memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "About Levi he said: 'Your Thummim and Urim belong to the man you favored. You tested him at Massah; you contended with him at the waters of Meribah... He teaches your precepts to Jacob and your law to Israel. He offers incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar. Bless all his skills, Lord, and be pleased with the work of his hands.'" — Deut 33:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The blessing on Levi celebrates a tribe set apart for a special calling: to teach God's law and to serve at His altar. "He teaches your precepts to Jacob... He offers incense before you." The Levites were the priests and teachers of Israel, devoted to God's service. Moses prays that God would bless their work and be pleased with the labour of their hands. Their whole lives were given to helping others know and worship God.

There is something worth pondering here about the dignity of serving God and helping others draw near to Him. The Levites had no ordinary inheritance of land; the Lord Himself was their portion. Their calling was to point people to God — through teaching His Word and leading in worship. It was a life of sacred service.

While the Levitical priesthood belonged to that particular covenant era, the heart of this calling continues for all God's people. In Christ, all believers are called "a royal priesthood" (1 Pet 2:9), set apart to know God and to help others know Him. Every one of us can teach God's truth in some measure, and every one of us can offer the "incense" of prayer and praise.

And behind every earthly priest stands our great High Priest, Jesus, who perfectly offered Himself and now intercedes for us (Heb 7:25). The Levites pointed forward to Him. So embrace your calling to serve God and help others find Him. Whatever your work, offer it to God, and let Him be pleased with the labour of your hands as you point people toward the great High Priest.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see my life as set apart to know God and help others know Him?
2. How can I "teach God's precepts" and offer prayer and praise where I am?
3. What work of my hands can I offer to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for calling me into Your priesthood, set apart to know You and help others draw near. Bless the work of my hands, and use me to point people to Christ, our great High Priest. Amen.
